subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw expose these three independent opt-in Gateway security toggles in core, rather than keeping WebSocket hardening within the established origin/trusted-proxy policy surfaces?
rationale: This is a durable security and configuration product boundary: code review can assess the mechanics, but maintainers must choose the supported operator posture and long-term configuration contract.

options.title: Approve the opt-in security surface
options.body: Keep the three settings, add public Gateway documentation and final-head wire proof for both strict rejection and trusted-proxy compatibility.

options.title: Narrow to an existing policy surface
options.body: Reduce the proposal to behavior already owned by the established browser-origin or trusted-proxy configuration contract and avoid a new `gateway.security` group.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in security surface
recommendation.body: Keep the three settings, add public Gateway documentation and final-head wire proof for both strict rejection and trusted-proxy compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The available timeline provides the only direct evidence of an early decision participant for this Gateway security proposal.
